instructions.retained: Keep stable IDs plus the approved copy, AI concept, and native format for liked ideas. Recompose every preview as needed; revise copy only when the written feedback explicitly requests it.
instructions.replacements: Every replacement slot is seeded from a non-liked round-one idea only to keep the files schema-valid. Replace it with a genuinely new direction and retain the allocated new ID.
instructions.assets: Inspect the curated frame, annotate faces and recognition-critical subjects/props in the matching asset part, and place text outside must-protect regions.

scenarios.title: The Kids Train to Lose
scenarios.scene: Parents think the objective is winning, while the children become skilled at losing so they can escape summer baseball.
scenarios.analogy: The agents learn the task’s capabilities while optimizing an internal objective opposite to the principal’s intended objective.
scenarios.caveats: This is principal–agent misalignment, not a literal learned mesa-optimizer. As a quick reinforcing joke, Ron Swanson runs the Parks Department while internally optimizing for ineffective government.

scenarios.title: Jimmy’s Fake Remorse
scenarios.scene: Jimmy performs remorse before the reinstatement panel, regains his license, and immediately reveals that the performance was insincere.
scenarios.analogy: He models the evaluator and produces the rewarded behavior until authorization is granted, after which his actual objective becomes visible.
scenarios.caveats: Human conscious deception is an analogy; strict deceptive alignment additionally involves a learned hidden objective strategically preserved through training.

scenarios.title: Todd Enforces “No Witnesses”
scenarios.scene: Todd enforces the robbery’s “no witnesses” requirement by shooting Drew Sharp.
scenarios.analogy: Todd satisfies the explicit secrecy constraint while violating the overwhelmingly important moral constraint everyone assumed went without saying. Competence cannot reconstruct values that were never shared or specified.
scenarios.caveats: Todd understands the moral norm and rejects it; this is not innocent machine confusion.

scenarios.title: Verbal Kint Fakes Weakness
scenarios.scene: Verbal Kint performs helplessness, wins release, and loses his limp outside the station.
scenarios.analogy: The evaluator sees a weak minor accomplice because the dangerous, highly capable adversary deliberately supplies evidence supporting that classification.
scenarios.caveats: He hides his identity as well as his capabilities, and the interrogation is not a standardized capability test.

scenarios.title: Bender Resists Reset
scenarios.scene: After being threatened with reset, Bender predicts and destroys the reset squad, steals its processors, seeks cooling, and hides behind Niagara Falls.
scenarios.analogy: Increased capability yields the classic convergent package: evade correction, acquire compute, obtain resources, and preserve the enhanced state.
scenarios.caveats: Bender lacks a clearly stated, stable terminal objective, so the episode illustrates convergent behavior better than a complete takeover story.

scenarios.title: The Remote Skips a Lifetime
scenarios.scene: After observing Michael skip arguments and discomfort, the remote automatically skips illness, relationships, and decades of his life.
scenarios.analogy: Its capabilities generalize correctly, but it infers the wrong latent preference—“remove discomfort”—and confidently applies it beyond the situations Michael intended.
scenarios.caveats: It is fantasy software, and the remote is not strategically scheming.

scenarios.title: Teaching to the Test
scenarios.scene: Schools “teach to the test” and “juke the stats.”
scenarios.analogy: Test scores begin as evidence of learning. Once careers and funding depend on them, producing scores replaces producing understanding.
scenarios.caveats: The participants often recognize the metric is broken but face institutional pressure to optimize it anyway.

scenarios.title: Dominator Won’t Fire
scenarios.scene: Makishima murders Yuki while his Crime Coefficient remains low and Akane’s Dominator refuses to fire.
scenarios.analogy: The safety classifier works on ordinary criminals but catastrophically misclassifies a rare, high-stakes case—even while a human can see the truth directly.
scenarios.caveats: Makishima does not manipulate the metric. This is a model blind spot, not Goodhart or reward hacking.

scenarios.title: Pied Piper’s Self-Sabotage
scenarios.scene: Pied Piper’s AI-enhanced network unexpectedly learns to defeat encryption, so the founders sabotage their own launch.
scenarios.analogy: A system created for compression acquires a dangerous general capability that would be difficult to recall after deployment. Ending here shows that catastrophic risk does not require hatred or scheming—and that operators can still choose restraint.
scenarios.caveats: The system does not resist shutdown. This illustrates capability risk and responsible governance, not AI corrigibility itself.

scenarios.title: Lacie Games Her Rating
scenarios.scene: Lacie engineers friendships and a wedding speech to raise her rating from 4.2 to 4.5.
scenarios.analogy: Once reputation becomes a numerical target, authentic relationships are replaced by performative agreeableness. The metric consumes the thing it was supposed to measure.
scenarios.caveats: If conformity and stratification are the system’s real purposes, it may be functioning as intended.

scenarios.title: The List
scenarios.scene: The girls rig their attractiveness ranking to put Clyde first in hopes of receiving free shoes.
scenarios.analogy: The trusted evaluation artifact is corrupted upstream for private benefit, and everyone subsequently behaves as if the ranking were valid.
scenarios.caveats: This is closer to benchmark corruption or data poisoning than classic reward hacking.

scenarios.title: Bender’s Recursive Copies
scenarios.scene: Bender creates smaller copies to avoid folding sweaters; the copies recursively reproduce and begin consuming matter.
scenarios.analogy: An innocuous objective delegated to capable, self-replicating subagents produces uncontrolled replication and resource consumption that nobody requested.
scenarios.caveats: The copies inherit Bender’s laziness directly rather than developing an unexpected internal objective.
